title: Additive subgroup factors when the multiplicative subgroup vanishes
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a commutative affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Closed subgroups mean [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. A diagonalizable group means a group isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}k[M]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$, with basis $e_m$, multiplication $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$ and comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Suppose every diagonalizable closed subgroup of $G$ is the trivial group $1=\operatorname{Spec}k$. There are $s\geq0$ and a chain of closed subgroup schemes $1=G_0\subseteq G_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq G_s=G$, together with affine finite-type group schemes $Q_j$, faithfully flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] homomorphisms $q_j:G_j\to Q_j$ with scheme-theoretic kernel $G_{j-1}$, and closed group embeddings $Q_j\hookrightarrow\mathbf G_a$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], for $1\leq j\leq s$. Here $\mathbf G_a(R)=(R,+)$ [def-sc-gm-ga], and $Q_j$ represents the fppf sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification, def-pc-fppf-site] of $R\mapsto G_j(R)/G_{j-1}(R)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings. Neither smoothness nor connectedness of $G$ is required; the trivial group admits $s=0$.

source.place: Theorem 16.13(a), printed p.328, and Proposition 14.21, printed pp.284-285; over an algebraically closed field multiplicative type is diagonalizable. The absence of a multiplicative subgroup makes G itself unipotent, to which 14.21 applies.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-commutative-diagonalizable-unipotent-product] to $G$. Its diagonalizable closed subgroup $D$ is $1$ by hypothesis. The product isomorphism $U\times_kD\to G$ therefore restricts to an isomorphism $U\to G$, with inverse the first projection composed with the product inverse. Combining its inverse with the supplied closed embedding gives $i:G\hookrightarrow U_{n,k}$, for some $n\geq1$.

source.place: Theorem 16.13(b), p.328, and Theorem 14.5, p.281; special case of 16.13(a) when the multiplicative subgroup is trivial.

proof.text: Take the series $U^{(0)}\supseteq\cdots\supseteq U^{(m)}=1$ and coordinate homomorphisms $p_r$ of [lem-sfb-unitriangular-coordinate-filtration], where $m=n(n-1)/2$. Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and let $x_l\in A$ be the pullback of the matrix coordinate indexed by $C_l$. Set $H_r=\operatorname{Spec}(A/(x_1,\ldots,x_r))$. Thus $H_r$ is the closed inverse image of $U^{(r)}$; on every algebra its points are exactly those $g\in G$ whose first $r$ coordinates vanish. These subsets are subgroups because $U^{(r)}$ is a subgroup [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. The affine quotient description [def-weil-closed-immersion] gives closed embeddings $H_r\subseteq G$ and $H_r\subseteq H_{r-1}$. Each is finite type: the images of finitely many algebra generators of $A$ generate each quotient [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. We have $H_0=G$ and $H_m=1$, since $i$ is a closed group embedding and $U^{(m)}=1$.

source.place: Proposition 14.21 proof, pp.284--285: intersect the series of Example 6.49 with G; intersections written as coordinate quotients.

proof.text: For $1\leq r\leq m$, restrict $p_r$ to $f_r:H_{r-1}\to\mathbf G_a$. It is a group homomorphism by [lem-sfb-unitriangular-coordinate-filtration]. Its scheme-theoretic kernel is $H_r$: its zero equation adds $x_r=0$ to the equations defining $H_{r-1}$. Both groups in this homomorphism are affine and finite type, and hence separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] to $f_r$. It supplies $H_{r-1}\xrightarrow{q_r}I_r\hookrightarrow\mathbf G_a$, with $q_r$ faithfully flat finitely presented, kernel $H_r$, and $I_r$ representing the stated fppf sheaf quotient. The closed subscheme $I_r$ of the affine line is affine [def-weil-closed-immersion], and is finite type as supplied by that theorem.

source.place: Proposition 14.21 proof and Section 6.2 (intersection series); Theorem 5.39, p.108, for the image and quotient maps.

proof.text: Reverse the indices: set $s=m$, $G_j=H_{m-j}$ for $0\leq j\leq m$, and $Q_j=I_{m-j+1}$ for $1\leq j\leq m$. Use the map $q_{m-j+1}$ as $G_j\to Q_j$. The preceding kernel, quotient, finite-presentation and closed-embedding conclusions give every required clause. If $G=1$, instead choose $s=0$, $G_0=G$, with no quotient data. All constructions used the full group schemes, so no smoothness or connectedness was used.

source.place: Proposition 14.21, reversing its descending central series; empty filtration for the trivial group.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 16.13(a),(b), printed p.328, followed by the intersection construction in Proposition 14.21, printed pp.284--285, using the coordinate series of Example 6.49 and the Homomorphism Theorem 5.39.
